description: Predicates a ProposalDraft may use. Wikidata mappings say which source statements can evidence each predicate: forward means the statement's entity is the assertion subject; inverse means the statement's value is the assertion subject. v2: commanded relates a person to a force (Group), not to an event. v3: authority held over a force (heldAuthorityOver) is separated from command actually exercised (commanded); evidence for one never counts for the other. v4: each predicate declares its qualifiers (context, role, time: none, optional, required, or withRole for time required only when a role is given) and its claim modes; adds the unary occurred and authorOf (22-CLAIM-QUALIFIERS.md). v5: each predicate declares a category (factual or interpretive); kinds Office and Concept; narrative links triggeredBy and resultedIn; interpretive exemplifies and ledTo (attributed only) and depictsSameAs (curator) (23-NARRATIVE-AND-NOTES.md). v6: occurred extends to Period (each source's bounds an attributed claim); subperiodOf and followedBy relate periods; partOf stays Event to Event (24-PERIODS-AND-TRANSFORMATION.md). v7: opposed relates people or groups who were opponents, symmetric, time required, with an optional context event (the war or battle); political, military, or personal opposition is not split. Works carry a form; a claim attributed to a Work of a creative form is imaginative, derived and never chosen (25-LIVES-AND-PLAYGROUND.md section 6). v8: born and died are dated unary claims (no date is a bare property; 25 section 10), from Wikidata P569 and P570; participatedIn also maps P1344 (participant in). v9 (2026-10-13; docs/Response - Roman Republican Institutions and Military Hierarchies.md): kinds Type (unit types, organizational patterns, roles, powers) and Polity (states); partOf extended to Groups and Types, its endpoint kinds paired (kindPairs) so an event is never part of a group; instanceOf, precedes, electedBy, exercisedPower, heldPower, servedUnder, memberOf; a quantity qualifier (minimum, maximum, typical) on partOf and electedBy; context and role kinds per predicate (contextKinds, roleKinds; defaults Event and the roleKind). P361 on a Person and P463 map to memberOf; which predicate a P361 statement evidences follows from its endpoints' kinds. Facts that happen once (once: true: born, died, occurred, bornAt, diedAt, occurredAt) are disputed when their sources give different times, places, contexts, or roles; any other fact may recur (two consulships, two marriages), so such differences are separate occasions, not a dispute. occurred extended to Polity: a state's existence, by each source's dates. v10 (2026-10-15; 29-EVENT-CENTRED-INQUIRY.md, 23-NARRATIVE-AND-NOTES.md section 2): happenedBefore orders events as a source narrates them (Event to Event, no time: the order itself is the content); it is separate from precedes, the dated order of offices. occurred takes an optional context event, so a depicted event's time marker can be anchored to the event it happens within (a relative offset). v11 (curator, 2026-10-15): participatedIn takes an optional time, so a participation is dated, or spanned from its start to its end, when the source or the Wikidata statement gives it; an undated participation stays undated. v12 (D-136): partOf also relates a Work to a Work (a Life within a collection). v13 (D-138, 2026-11-12; 39-LENS-SPECIALISTS.md): participatedIn takes a role of kind Office or Type, so the participants of an act carry the part the source gives them (captor, captured, deserter, hostage, envoy); roles of kind Type are Chrystallum entities like any other, reviewed before use. v14: involvedIn relates an Object to an Event it took part in only through a role it is required to carry (seized, dedicated, destroyed; a Type); participatedIn stays for agents (Group, Person, Polity), so who took part is never confused with what was taken (curator, 2026-11-12). No Wikidata mapping until one is checked at Wikidata. v15: a Type's typeCategory (D-039) comes from typeCategories: role, unit type, organizational pattern, power, or status (status added 2026-11-13: a recognised standing such as matrona, held rather than an office; a hadStatus predicate is requested in curation/predicate-needs.json). Also v15: a Wikidata mapping may carry a bound (start or end): the statement evidences that end of the claim's interval only (occurred: inception P571 or start time P580 for the start; dissolved P576 or end time P582 for the end), so one span claim rests on two statements. The deterministic proposer never drafts from a bound alone. v16 (curator, 2026-11-15; 43-ACTIUM-MILITARY-FRAME.md): hadStrength (a force numbered a count of ships or men at a time, by one source, never reconciled; the Type counted as its role), captured, surrenderedTo, defectedTo; a quantity may say its precision (exact, approximate, round, rhetorical); typeCategories add ship type and naval fitting; workForms add coinage (a coin series as a source, D-151). v17 (D-153, 44-HISTORIOGRAPHY-AND-DEBATES.md): kinds Question (a historical question scholars answer differently) and Position (one answer, shared by its holders); about (Question to the Event, Person, Group, Polity or Period it concerns), answers (Position to Question), holds and rejects (a Work argues for or against a Position: the Work, not its author, since a scholar may change their view; time when argued; holds takes an optional stance: originates, adopts, modifies), and the unary hadReception (how a Position stood in scholarship over a span: dominant, contested, minority, abandoned; always a voice's claim). All interpretive: an interpretation, ancient or modern, is never evidence for a fact, and how many held a view is never its attestation. The stance never makes a different claim; the reception does. v18 (45, D-160): animals, plants, metals and materials as Types (typeCategory taxon, material, product, denomination); subtypeOf (an authority's hierarchy), madeOf, struckIn, madeFrom, producedAt. v19 (45, D-160): colour as a Type category and hadColour (an object's colour, a link to a colour, never to a dye or a material); about may reach a Type (which modern species is Pliny's purpura). v20 (46, D-166): a Group's groupCategory, first value gens (a Roman clan); ofGens (Person to a Group of category gens: belonging to a clan for life, so no time, unlike memberOf; Wikidata P5025 gens); a predicate may require its object's category (objectCategories). Praenomen, nomen, cognomen and agnomen are properties of the Person, never entities.

predicates.definition: The person actually directed the force in action: led it, gave it orders, or fought at its head. Formal or supreme authority over a force is heldAuthorityOver, not commanded.
The person held formal or supreme authority over the force, whether or not they directed it in action. Directing it in action is commanded.
The two were opponents: rivals or enemies, in politics or at war. Give the war or battle as context when the passage names one. Feelings such as hatred or fear are passages of note, not this claim.

The subject is a component of the object: an event within a larger event, a force within a larger force (a wing of a fleet), a unit type within an organizational pattern (with a quantity: how many such units), or a work within a collection or larger work. A separate Work is not identical to its collection; membership is an evidence-bearing claim, not inferred from identity. Never an event within a period (period membership is computed) or a person within a group (memberOf).
The source presents the event as set off by the other event ("when he saw this").
The source presents the other event as an outcome of this one, within its narrative.

In the source's account the subject event takes place before the object event: the source says so ("then", "afterwards", "after this"), or gives times that order them. The order in which the source tells the events is not enough, and an event set off by another is triggeredBy, not only after it.
Two sources' depicted events are of one historical action. An identification made by the curator.
The period is conventionally treated as a part of the larger period.
The period is conventionally followed by the other period.

The event took place, the period lasted, or the state existed, over the time given by the claim's time qualifier. A unary claim: it has no object. For a period, each source's bounds are a separate attributed claim. A depicted event within a larger event may take that event as context, so its time marker ("at the sixth hour") can carry an offset from it.
When the person born: a unary claim whose content is its time. The place is a separate claim (bornAt).
When the person died: a unary claim whose content is its time. The place is a separate claim (diedAt).
The person composed the work. The time qualifier, when given, is the date of composition.
In the author's reading, the subject is an instance of the concept. An interpretation, always attributed.
In the author's reading, a long-range consequence of the event. An interpretation, always attributed; within a narrative use resultedIn.
A historical force or body is an instance of a type: a unit of a given pattern, a body of a given type. Dated where the type changed.
In the order of offices (the cursus), the subject comes before the object, as fixed at a time; the order and its rules changed, so the claim is dated.
Holders of the office are elected by the assembly, at a time; a quantity gives how many were elected.
The office carries a power as its competence, at a time.

A person held a power for a defined command within limits of time and task: the role is the office it was held through, the context the task, war, territory, or force it applied to. A power is never a permanent attribute: the claim is dated.
A person served under another's command, in a role and a context (a war or a force), at a time. Replaces edges between command assignments, which the model does not have.
A person belonged to a body: a college, an alliance, a council. Distinct from holding its office (heldPosition) and from an informal alliance between persons (alliedWith).

A force numbered a given count of ships or men at a time, as one source states it. Each source's figure is its own voice and is never reconciled with another's. The role names what is counted when the source says (a ship type such as quinquereme, or legions); without a role the count is of the source's own unit, as its words give it.
A force or person took enemy ships, men, or goods in an engagement. Give the engagement as context and the count as a quantity when the source gives one.
A force or person yielded to an enemy commander or force.
A person or force left one side and went over to the other. The object is the side or commander joined.

The question concerns this entity: what Antony meant to do at Actium is about the battle. A Question is reached one hop from what it is about. A Question may also be about a Type: which modern species an ancient name for a living thing names.
The position is one answer to the question. Several positions answer one question; a debate is rarely two-sided.

The work argues this position. The subject is the Work, not its author (one hop away through authorOf), since a scholar may change their view between works and an ancient author may be inconsistent within one. The time, when given, is when the work argued it; the stance, when the source says, whether the work originates the position, adopts it, or modifies it. Attributed to the Work that says so: a work stating its own view, or another reporting it (basis reports) until the holder is read. Never evidence for the fact the position concerns.
The work argues against this position. Like holds: the Work is the subject, the time is when it argued, and it is attributed to the Work that says so.

How the position stood in scholarship over a span, as a source describes it: dominant ("the dominant view ever since"), contested, minority, or abandoned. A unary claim; the span and the reception are its content. Always a voice's claim, never ours, and never a score of the position.

A kind of thing falls under a broader kind, as an authority's hierarchy places it: a species under its genus (GBIF Backbone Taxonomy), silver under nonferrous metal or the denarius under coins (Getty AAT). Always the authority's voice, from its record; the authority's organizing headings (AAT guide terms, hierarchy names, facets) are passed over, not made Types. Never a role or a unit pattern (partOf).

A thing, or a kind of thing, is made of a material: a denarius of silver, as the coin records give it; a sail of linen. The object is a Type of category material or product. A colour is not a material: it is a property of the object (45 §4.2).
A coinage (a Work of form coinage) was struck in a denomination (a Type of category denomination): Antony's legionary coinage in denarii and aurei, from its coin types' records.
A product is made from a source material or a living thing, as a source says: Tyrian purple from the murex. Not what a thing is made of (madeOf).
A product or material was produced, mined or gathered at a place, as a source says: murex purple at Tyre, silver at Laurion. Dated where the source dates it.

An object's colour, as a source gives it: Cleopatra's sails at Actium were purple (Pliny). The object is a Type of category colour (Getty AAT). A property of the object: it never says what the object was dyed with or made of (madeOf), which a source must state.

A person belonged to a Roman gens (clan), by birth or by adoption: Lucius Pinarius Scarpus was of the gens Pinaria. For life, so no time (memberOf requires one). An adopted person has two, each with its own source. The nomen is a word on the Person; the gens is the clan.
